title: Groundbreaking Transplant Restores Woman's Sight
paragraphs: An Italian woman who was blinded in an accident has regained sight in one of her eyes after getting a groundbreaking transplant using parts of her other eye.

The 67-year-old patient, named only as Elena, lost her eyesight in a road accident five years ago. The optic nerve in her left eye was completely severed, although the rest of that eye was left mostly healthy.
The accident also damaged the retina and cornea in her right eye, but the optic nerve of that eye was fine.
Now, surgeons at the Molinette Hospital in Turin have been able to use healthy parts from each of Elena's eyes to restore sight in her right eye.
The six-hour surgery involved the world's first transplant of a part of the eye called the macula.
Part of the retina, the macula is a 5 millimeter oval spot at the back of the eye that is responsible for most of our color and fine-detail vision.

The surgeons took Elena's healthy macula from her left eye and transplanted it to her right eye. They also transplanted her left eye's undamaged cornea, sclera — or the white of the eye — and conjunctiva, which is the thin membrane that covers the eye.
The result was one reconstructed, seeing eye.
Surgeon Michele Reibaldi said the team is now monitoring how well her reconstructed eye is working, but the early results are positive.
"The greatest reward for all of us was the incredible moment when Elena, opening her eyes again, was finally able to recognize the faces of her son and her faithful life partner, Joe," he said.
Joe is Elena's guide dog. He was given special permission to stay with Elena at Molinette Hospital because staff recognized the importance of the emotional support he provides.
